items.label: Reaction profile
items.clue: An energy diagram for a reaction.

items.label: Reaction pathway
items.clue: The route a reaction takes from reactants to products.

questions.stem: A student follows the reaction between marble chips and dilute hydrochloric acid, which gives off carbon dioxide. Which set of measurements would allow the mean rate of reaction to be worked out?

options.text: The volume of gas collected, together with the time taken to collect it
The total volume of gas given off at the end, and nothing else
The time taken until the fizzing finally stops, and nothing more
The temperature of the mixture, measured every ten seconds

questions.explanation: The rate of a chemical reaction can be found by measuring the quantity of product formed over time, so a quantity and a time are both needed.

questions.stem: In a reaction, 3.6 g of magnesium ribbon is used up in 180 s. What is the mean rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: mean rate of reaction = (quantity of reactant used) / (time taken) = 3.6 g / 180 s.

questions.stem: A gas syringe collects 12 cm³ of gas in 8 s. What is the mean rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: mean rate of reaction = (quantity of product formed) / (time taken) = 12 cm³ / 8 s.

questions.stem: The specification states how the quantity of a reactant or product may be measured. Which pair does it give?

options.text: The concentration in mol/dm³ or the temperature in °C
The mass in grams or the total time taken in seconds
The volume in cm³ or the pressure of the gas in pascals
The mass measured in grams or the volume in cm³

questions.explanation: The quantity of reactant or product can be measured by the mass in grams or by a volume in cm³ .

questions.stem: Which of these is given in the specification as a unit of rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: The units of rate of reaction may be given as g/s or cm³ /s.

questions.stem: A flask of reacting mixture stands on a balance. The mass falls from 82.50 g to 81.90 g in 120 s. What is the mean rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: The mass lost is 0.60 g, and 0.60 g divided by 120 s gives 0.0050 g/s.

questions.stem: Experiment X produces 30 cm³ of gas in 20 s. Experiment Y produces 45 cm³ of gas in 45 s. Which statement about the mean rates is correct?

options.text: Y is faster, because Y produces the larger total volume of gas
Y is faster, because the reaction in Y was allowed to run for longer
The mean rates are equal, since both experiments make gas steadily
X is faster: its mean rate is 1.5 cm³ /s and the mean rate of Y is 1.0 cm³ /s

questions.explanation: Each quantity is divided by its own time before the two are compared.

questions.stem: A graph of the volume of gas produced against time is steep at first and then becomes less steep. What does this shape show?

options.text: The volume of gas begins to fall once the curve bends over
The reaction speeds up steadily as more product forms
The reaction runs at one steady rate the whole way
The reaction is fastest at the start, and then slows down

questions.explanation: Steepness of the curve is a measure of rate, so a falling steepness means a falling rate.

questions.stem: The line on a graph of volume of gas against time becomes horizontal after 80 s. What does this tell you?

options.text: No more gas is being made, so the reaction has ended
Gas is now being made at a steady, constant rate
The reaction is still speeding up, but more gradually
The gas is now being used up again in a reverse reaction

questions.explanation: A horizontal line has zero gradient, so the rate is zero and the reaction has stopped.

questions.stem: A student needs the rate of reaction at 30 s from a curved graph of volume of gas against time. What should the student do?

options.text: Draw a tangent at 30 s and work out its slope
Read the volume off the curve at 30 s and use that
Join the origin to the point at 30 s and use that slope
Divide the final volume by the total time of the run

questions.explanation: The specification requires a tangent to be drawn and its slope used as a measure of the rate.

questions.stem: (HT) In a Higher Tier question the quantity of a reactant is given in moles. In which unit should the rate of reaction then be given?
questions.explanation: For the Higher Tier, units for rate of reaction may be given in mol/s.

questions.stem: (HT) In a reaction, 0.60 mol of hydrogen is produced in 30 s. What is the mean rate of reaction?
questions.explanation: 0.60 mol divided by 30 s, with the rate given in mol/s as the Higher Tier requires.

questions.stem: (HT) A tangent drawn to a volume-time curve at 20 s passes through the points (10 s, 12 cm³ ) and (30 s, 52 cm³ ). What is the rate of reaction at 20 s?
questions.explanation: The gradient is (52 - 12) cm³ divided by (30 - 10) s = 40 / 20 = 2.0 cm³ /s.
